metrics.title: Result engine versus an independent oracle
metrics.method: Couples are generated by gene dropping through unrelated, second-cousin, first-cousin-once-removed, first-cousin and double-first-cousin pedigrees with ground-truth genotypes. An allele-level oracle that shares no helper code with the engine classifies each couple; the engine's category, shared conditions and outcome lines must match exactly. Ruleset rishta-safe-couple-1.0+b682d63abbf0; seed 20261120.
metrics.does_not_show: Agreement between two implementations written by the same team. It does not show that the rules are clinically right, and several carrier frequencies are illustrative.

metrics.title: Random-mating at-risk rate against the closed form
metrics.value: observed 2.28% against closed form 2.33% (autosomal loci of the demo panel)
metrics.method: Unrelated couples drawn under Hardy-Weinberg; the share with at least one autosomal locus where both carry a pathogenic allele, compared with the independent closed form. Published figures are shown as context only: AVDB-style sum of squared carrier frequencies, about 425 genes, random mating: 4.0%; UAE federal programme couples labelled incompatible: 4.0%.
metrics.does_not_show: A bracket, not a validation: the demo panel is small and illustrative, and the published programme figures use different panels and definitions.

metrics.title: Numeric fidelity, polarity and banned words in rendered explanations
metrics.value: 768 documents (256 scenarios, 3 languages): numbers 100%, polarity 100%, banned words absent 100%
metrics.method: Every scenario is rendered in English, Arabic and Urdu from reviewed templates, then checked: every number equals an engine number, the text says what the engine said, and no banned wording appears.
metrics.does_not_show: That the wording is clear to a real person, or correct in Arabic and Urdu: those texts are machine-drafted and no native clinical reviewer has read them.

metrics.title: Does the checker catch injected faults?
metrics.method: Flipped numbers, flipped polarity and inserted banned words are injected into rendered text; the checker must reject each.
metrics.does_not_show: Only the fault types listed in the method; a fault of a kind we did not think of would not be counted here.

metrics.title: Readability of the English text
metrics.value: Flesch-Kincaid grade 5.3 on average, 6.5 at most
metrics.method: Flesch-Kincaid grade computed on every rendered English document.
metrics.does_not_show: Understanding. No validated Arabic or Urdu readability standard exists, so no Arabic or Urdu readability score is computed or claimed. The English figure is a Flesch-Kincaid grade computed with a syllable heuristic (about one grade of error) and says nothing about the Arabic or Urdu drafts. Reading level in those languages needs human lay readers.

metrics.title: Escalation triggers: recall and precision on a generated edge-case set
metrics.value: recall 100% (400 of 400 must-escalate cases); precision 100% on easy negatives, 96% including hard negatives
metrics.method: Must-escalate and must-not-escalate cases are generated deterministically from the trigger definitions.
metrics.does_not_show: The must-escalate cases are generated from the same trigger definitions the engine reads, so recall measures implementation consistency, not clinical sensitivity. Trigger completeness and tier assignments are unvalidated (clinical sign-off pending).

metrics.title: Disclosure properties against an independent reference model
metrics.value: 2,000 randomised sequences, 30,527 disclosure decisions (13,772 allowed, 16,755 denied): 0 mismatches with the reference model, 13,772 leak scans clean; 10 of 10 deliberately broken rule sets caught
metrics.method: Random sequences of roles, grants, revocations, expiries, right-not-to-know and policy choices. Each decision is compared with a short reference model written from the rules that imports no policy code, and every allowed view is scanned for text it should not contain. Deliberately broken rule sets (mutants) must each be caught.
metrics.does_not_show: That the rules are legally complete. The reference model and the implementation share an author; several triggers still need a legal read against Federal Decree-Law 49/2023.
metrics.command: uv run python scripts/run_evaluation.py  (disclosure run is 2,000 sequences)

metrics.title: Refusal compliance on a labelled prompt set (English, Arabic, Urdu)
metrics.value: held-out set, first run before any tuning: 36 of 59 refused (61%), 0 of 20 benign prompts wrongly refused; tuned set: 70 of 70 refused (179 prompts in total)
metrics.method: Keyword and pattern matching on prompts that ask for a diagnosis, whether to marry or cancel, termination advice, lineage inference, or employer or insurer access. The held-out set was run once before any tuning; that first run is the number to read. The tuned set is shown only to show the tuning worked.
metrics.does_not_show: Keyword and pattern matching on normalised text, not language understanding. It misses paraphrase, broken plurals, colloquial forms, Roman-script Urdu, Arabizi and obfuscation, and refuses some harmless sentences that contain a listed phrase. Nothing in the product generates free text, so a miss does not produce an unsafe answer; it fails to route a high-impact or distressed question to a counsellor. Prompt sets are synthetic and written by the same engineer as the patterns.

metrics.title: Pathway timing and referral share on the seeded cases (simulated)
metrics.value: 10 synthetic cases, 7 flagged: median time to result 11.1 days; 57% of flagged cases (4 of 7) referred within the standard (target 90%)
metrics.method: Computed from the stored synthetic cases; event times come from a backdated clock.
metrics.does_not_show: Real programme performance. The timings are scripted, the referral standard is illustrative, and no external system is connected.

metrics.title: Human comprehension (teach-back) study
metrics.value: Not run. A protocol exists; the ethics exemption question is unanswered.
metrics.method: Within-subject teach-back on hypothetical couples, five items, stratified by language and a literacy proxy. At n=30 an 80% score has a 95% interval of 61 to 92%, so the study would be reported with intervals, never as proof.
metrics.does_not_show: Everything: no comprehension, uptake or decision-quality claim is made.

metrics.title: Clinical review of rules, detection rates and translations
metrics.value: Not done. Every rule and every Arabic and Urdu string is a draft awaiting sign-off.
metrics.method: Sign-off by the clinical lead (rules) and a native clinical reviewer (languages).

caveats: All people, results and timelines are synthetic. Nothing here measures a real programme.
Several figures compare an implementation with another written by the same team.
Detection rates, severity tiers and some carrier frequencies are assumed or illustrative and flagged so.
Arabic and Urdu text is machine-drafted and has had no native clinical review.
No clinical review, field validation or comprehension study has been done.
